- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early periods of strong sentiment shifts; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mid-periods when sentiment is mixed; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to middle 10–15 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth transitions by averaging adjacent sentiment values before forecasting.
